slides.texte_overlay:
5 ways your posture quietly
ruins your presence in public
1: slouching while you wait. In queues, at the bus stop, in reception. People see you long before you speak. Stand tall even when nobody is talking to you.
2: holding your phone at belly level. Your head drops and your shoulders roll forward for hours. Lift the screen higher, or better, put it away.
3: walking with your hands in your pockets. It closes your body and slows your stride. Let your arms swing naturally and you instantly look more alive.
4: leaning back too far in your chair. It looks bored and careless in meetings. Sit upright, slightly forward, and you look engaged and confident.
5: tense, clenched fists. When you're nervous, your hands give it away first. Keep your fingers relaxed and open, resting on the table or by your sides.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A curious, settled mind shows up in a calmer and more open body.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. A curious, settled mind shows up in a calmer, more open body.

slides.texte_overlay: The fix: check your reflection in shop windows. Every time you pass one, roll your shoulders back and lift your chin. Small reminders like this add up fast, and after a few weeks good posture becomes your default.
